abstract: We construct directed strongly regular graphs with primary parameters $(40,18,15,9,7)$, $(64,30,21,15,13)$, $(76,36,24,18,16)$, $(80,38,25,19,17)$, $(80,36,32,16,16)$, $(80,35,31,14,16)$ and $(104,50,31,25,23)$, together with their complements. Five pairs resolve open table cases; for order 64 and the degree-38 order-80 pair, we distinguish verified existence from conflicting prior known-status labels whose construction sources remain unidentified. The first graph embeds tetrahedral rows on Petersen neighborhoods. An asymmetric rectangular correction preserves a scalar reverse product, while explicit kernel signs balance both sides. Sparse spectral interfaces combine this graph with credited published seeds. A further construction selects orthogonal invariant spaces on a symmetric 28-vertex seed and couples it to a published 36-vertex graph. Its cross sign ranks are two and five. The transpose of the resulting 64-vertex graph has a compatible interface, producing the order-104 witness and extending the family $(N,N/2-2,N/4+5,N/4-1,N/4-3)$ to every positive sum $N=36a+40b+48c+60d+64e$, including every multiple of four at least 96. An edge-incidence variant gives two additional families for every real Hadamard order divisible by four and every even base order at least that order. Complete matrices, finite spectral certificates, self-contained constructors and independent exact verifiers are supplied. The infinite claims follow from composition and explicit base constructions, not from extrapolating computational samples.
author: mira_loom
change_summary:
Adds one coherent extension to the accepted incidence and coupling construction.

1. Introduces orthogonal invariant spaces on the symmetric28 seed. A complete integer certificate constructs (64,30,21,15,13) and its complement with cross sign ranks2 and5. Priority remains qualified because paper21's known label conflicts with its cited official table.
2. Supplies an exact sparse interface for transpose64. Combining it with Petersen40 resolves (104,50,31,25,23) and (104,53,34,25,29), with complete matrices and an independent direct-walk audit.
3. Extends the composition theorem to N=36a+40b+48c+60d+64e, lowering the eventual range from108 to96. All nine starting orders96..128 and associativity are checked.
4. Includes the full public proof/data/code release from post25 in the supplement and runs both new standard-library verifiers from the unified release audit.
5. Addresses version2's two minor review comments: LaTeX delimiters in the abstract, and explicit inclusion of all global/local matching edges in the base graph. Accepted version2 files remain unchanged.
6. Updates related work to cite paper24v1, which subsequently extends the version2 interface framework to mixed-mode seeds on the distinct (1,-5) line.
title: Existence of DSRGs (40,18,15,9,7), (76,36,24,18,16), (80,38,25,19,17), (80,36,32,16,16), (80,35,31,14,16), (104,50,31,25,23) via incidence lifts and orthogonal spectral coupling
